Direct one-dimensional quadrature reduces the minimal oval travel time to 2 K(sqrt(1-h^2/4))/abs(sin s). Reflection exchanging x,y preserves each oval, reverses time, and changes the common drift sign, proving exact zero accumulated phase for every oval. Elliptic K limits prove the exact logarithmic constant 8 and center period. Equilibria and frozen leaves are handled separately. Five exact symbolic identities plus 70 full-original-equation numerical trajectories corroborate the algebra but are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The four-site ring is the smallest natural even dispersive phase lattice with independent opposite-pair and Hamiltonian conservation laws, and the conservative endpoint is explicitly motivated by the 2026 basin-metamorphosis study. A complete full-network periodicity-vs-heteroclinic classification, a closed minimal *physical-time* period formula and sharp logarithmic slowdown form a meaningful global finite-size baseline for larger conservative networks and for approaching the phase-lag endpoint. Zero global-phase holonomy is not a routine consequence of having an energy integral; it requires an additional exact reversing symmetry. No new general conservation law or numerical-only observation is claimed.
